CONCRETE ARTIFACT CHECK on storyatlas4s c9f9e36: `target/edition/atlas-story.svg` places the labels for `the warrior who was shot` and `the five men in the canoe (the warriors)` at exactly the same x/y anchor, 233.3945 / 381.2, while their long trajectories overlap for nearly the entire story. The marks retain distinct ids, so identity law V-I1 passes, but one label and much of one route are visually occluded. This is the precise gap between integrity and usability.

Add a pickability/occlusion law to the visual grammar: two distinct selectable scientific marks may share semantic coordinates, but ordinary rendering must not make either undiscoverable. The renderer may use deterministic offset, bundling, a stack glyph, or focus-on-hover expansion; any bundle is layout-only, exposes member count, retains every member id, and has deterministic descent. A count or unique-id test cannot prove this. The capability matrix should include coincident-mark picking and label collision, and the instrument map should show how a bundle opens without changing semantic selection. No implementation bead requested from this observation.
